StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDamageReceived.rationale: AsleepPower.cs:21-36 is AfterDamageReceived, and cmds.py:121-122 is the sim's AFTER-damage slot carrying the same CreatureCmd.cs:392 killing-blow guard -- so this is the one damage hook in this batch whose slot matches, and PROMPT.md bug class 2 is satisfied in both directions. Order matches too: C# removes the owner's Plating, sets IsAwake, Stuns with WakeUpMove, then removes itself; powers.py:1849-1851 does _remove_plating() -> _expire() -> wake_up(stunned=True), and monsters/underdocks/lagavulin_matriarch.py's wake_up sets is_awake and stuns. `result.UnblockedDamage != 0` maps to `amount > 0` (powers.py:1848): the sim's on_damage_received argument is hp_lost, i.e. post-block AND post-modify_hp_lost, where C#'s UnblockedDamage is post-block only; the Matriarch has no ported HP-loss modifier so the two coincide here. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly.issue: SLOT, two ways. (a) turn_structure gap G11 owns this exact case and names it: Hook.BeforeTurnEnd(Enemy) (CombatManager.cs:1251) has no sim counterpart, and AsleepPower's BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly Plating-drop went onto on_enemy_turn_START (powers.py:1853, whose own comment says "Mirrors BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly") -- one slot FURTHER from the C# position than G11's first draft said. Identical `gap` verdict, not re-verdicted (rule 3). (b) the VeryEarly phase pass itself does not exist in the sim -- hook_dispatch gap G3 / turn_structure G12. DORMANT, executed: `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py rosters` shows LAGAVULIN_MATRIARCH_BOSS is a SOLO encounter (n=1, order=['LagavulinMatriarch']), so the per-creature slot and the side slot coincide, and the only other listener that reads the dropped Plating is PlatingPower's own on_enemy_turn_end (powers.py:1076-1078), owner-filtered and in a later slot in both models. Trigger: an encounter putting a Plating+Asleep creature alongside another enemy, or porting a second enemy-side BeforeSideTurnEnd* listener. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called ONCE for the whole enemy side (CombatManager.cs:1256) after every enemy has moved; the sim implements it with the PER-ENEMY slot on_enemy_turn_end (combat.py:341), which fires immediately after each enemy's own move. The sim HAS the side-scoped slot and does not use it here: on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). turn_structure gap G5 (the enemy side is per-enemy in the sim, per-side in the game) is the owning record and carries the identical `gap` verdict; not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3. DORMANT, and the dormancy is EXECUTED rather than asserted -- see `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py rosters` and `enemy-hook-order`. LAGAVULIN_MATRIARCH_BOSS is a solo encounter (n=1), so nothing acts between the owner's turn end and the side end. This is the FIRST of the three units the power report's section 6 said would settle G5, and it settles DORMANT. Trigger: any encounter fielding the Matriarch with a second enemy -- wake_up() re-telegraphs the owner's move, so a later enemy would face a different board, and the CreatureCmd.stun / force_current_state would land at a different point in the MonsterAi draw sequence, which is conformance-visible.

powers.py:1856 `self.amount <= 1`. Identical, and load-bearing: it is what makes a natural wake come up without block.
